task.description: WF-02 Step 3b: hard gate on TEST-DESIGNER's REQ-376 test spec + test code. Verify every AC/EO test shape is actually exercised, verify the genuine :pending_detach induction technique is reliable (not merely asserted), verify AC2/EO-001's no-per-row-DELETE query-log scoping, verify the §4.4b batching test genuinely exercises >1 batch with a properly-scoped/restored override, and verify the tenant_fixture.ex predicate is narrowly scoped and not masking a real defect.
acceptance_criteria: Every REQ-376 executable AC/EO has >=1 runnable test, not merely asserted as a side effect
The :pending_detach induction is independently re-run and confirmed reliable, not flaky
AC2/EO-001's query-log capture is confirmed to correctly exclude/not-be-confounded-by step 1's legitimate queries
The §4.4b batching override is confirmed to exercise >=2 batches and is properly restored
tenant_fixture.ex's req376_partition_management_table?/1 is confirmed narrowly scoped, not masking a real tenant-provisioning defect

result.summary:
Read the spec (test/specs/REQ-376.md), the ~860-line test file in full, the support-infra diff (test/support/tenant_fixture.ex, test/support/tenant_template.ex, test/letflow/support/tenant_fixture_test.exs via `git diff main...HEAD`), decision 0037 (ACCEPTED, with its Implementation-discovered-corrections section), the amended design doc in full, and lib/letflow/event_store/partition_maintenance.ex in full, before running anything.

Compile check: `MIX_ENV=test mix compile --warnings-as-errors --force` -- clean, 'Compiling 282 files (.ex) / Generated letflow app', zero warnings. TEST-DESIGNER's own compile confirmation is real.

Static review of coverage mapping (test/specs/REQ-376.md's 13 cases against the design doc's own §8 coverage map and §4.3.3/§4.5/§6 test shapes) found no gap: all 4 executable ACs, all 5 catalog_state/2 branches, both REVIEWER-accepted corrections, and both error cases each have a dedicated `test` block, not folded into another test's assertions as an incidental side effect. tenant_fixture.ex's req376_partition_management_table?/1 diff was read in full: it is applied only at the two named call sites (tenant_template.ex's template_self_check!/1 'extra' side, tenant_fixture_test.exs's C6 oracle-rot test), @expected_tenant_tables itself and Letflow.Test.TenantTemplate's do_clone/2 loop are untouched, and the reasoning (CREATE TABLE LIKE ... INCLUDING ALL does not copy PARTITION BY, so a :clone-provisioned tenant never has these artifacts) is correct and doesn't mask a real provisioning defect -- this part of TEST-DESIGNER's work is sound.

BLOCKING: task instruction #2 required independently re-deriving whether the :pending_detach induction technique is actually reliable, not merely asserted -- this cannot be done by reading code alone (core-directives.md's 're-derive under the conditions the property is actually about'), so I ran the actual test file against the real Postgres 16 instance already running for this workspace (docker container letflow-postgres-1, port 5462, matching config/test.exs) three times, with three different --seed values (0, 1, 42) to vary ExUnit's execution order:

  MIX_ENV=test mix test test/letflow/event_store/partition_maintenance_test.exs --seed 0
  MIX_ENV=test mix test test/letflow/event_store/partition_maintenance_test.exs --seed 1
  MIX_ENV=test mix test test/letflow/event_store/partition_maintenance_test.exs --seed 42

All three runs: identical result, Result: 10/13 passed, Failed: 3 tests -- the SAME three tests every time:

1. 'resumed from :pending_detach, a genuinely interrupted DETACH CONCURRENTLY' -- FAILED all 3/3 runs, with two DIFFERENT failure modes across the three runs (seed 0: retire_month/3 returned resumed_from: :detached_standalone instead of :pending_detach -- the DETACH CONCURRENTLY had already fully completed by the time retire_month/3 ran, meaning the interrupted state was never reached; seed 1 and seed 42: 'pending-detach state did not persist after interrupting the detach' -- the first wait_until succeeded but pending_detach?/2 went false again after the Task.shutdown(:brutal_kill)). Root cause: the holder Task (started via bare Task.start/1, no handshake) has no guarantee its Repo.transaction/1 has actually opened and taken a snapshot before the detacher Task's DETACH ... CONCURRENTLY begins -- both are independently scheduled BEAM processes with no synchronization between 'holder launched' and 'holder's transaction is actually open'. This is exactly the flakiness risk this gate's task instructions named, and it is not hypothetical -- it reproduced in 3/3 real runs against real Postgres 16, never once succeeding. The test's own moduledoc/inline comments claim this induces the state 'not merely asserted/simulated' and 'reliably' -- that claim does not hold as implemented.

2. 'EO-002 ... a keep_forever row's count across events UNION events_archive is unchanged' -- FAILED all 3/3 runs, deterministically (same Postgrex error every time): `** (Postgrex.Error) ERROR 23514 (check_violation) updated partition constraint for default partition "events_archive_default" would be violated by some row`, raised from attach_partition!/4 (partition_maintenance.ex:582) inside do_detached_standalone/7 -- i.e. step 4's ATTACH PARTITION itself fails. This is NOT test flakiness -- it is a genuine, reproducible implementation defect, and the design doc's own text explains why: §4.4's step 1 runs 4.4b (events_archive_default reconciliation) BEFORE 4.4a (keep_forever relocation) specifically 'so 4.4a's keep_forever rows then land in events_archive_default and simply stay there ... rather than round-tripping' -- but that is exactly what step 4's ATTACH precondition (stated in the SAME design doc, §4.3.3 step 4: 'requires events_archive_default to hold no row matching the target range at the moment of ATTACH ... which is exactly what step 1's reconciliation guarantees ahead of this step') forbids: a keep_forever row relocated by 4.4a into events_archive_default for the target month's own range is still sitting there, in-range, when step 4's ATTACH runs immediately afterward, so Postgres correctly refuses the ATTACH. The design's own two sentences contradict each other for exactly the EO-002 fixture shape (a keep_forever row whose created_at falls inside the month being retired) -- this is a real, load-bearing gap between the design and the implementation that the test correctly caught; it is not evidence against the test, it is evidence the test is doing its job. But it means AC3/EO-002 is NOT currently satisfied by lib/letflow/event_store/partition_maintenance.ex as shipped.

3. 'correction (a) -- events_default self-heals ... a far-future write still lands there' -- FAILED all 3/3 runs, deterministically: `** (DBConnection.EncodeError) Postgrex expected a binary of 16 bytes, got "<uuid string>"`, at test/letflow/event_store/partition_maintenance_test.exs:794 -- the test's own raw-SQL tableoid lookup (`Repo.query!(~s{... WHERE event_id = $1}, [event.event_id])`) passes event.event_id as its string form, but Repo.query!/3 (raw SQL, bypassing Ecto.Query's schema-driven type casting) requires a genuine 16-byte binary for a uuid-typed bind parameter. This is a straightforward bug IN THE TEST CODE, not flakiness and not an implementation defect -- it will fail on every single run, deterministically, regardless of correctness of the events_default self-heal behavior the test claims to prove. The test as written can never pass and can never actually validate REVIEWER correction (a).

All raw logs saved under this session's scratchpad if a re-check is needed (not committed -- ephemeral verification artifacts per core-directives.md's scratch rule).

Conclusion: this is not a 'looks reasonable, no real check performed' situation -- I independently re-ran the actual suite against real Postgres, three times, with varied seeds, specifically to test the claim this gate's task instructions told me to verify, and the claim does not hold: 3 of 13 tests (23%) fail on every run. Per Step 3b's own acceptance check (a) ('at least one runnable test targets it') -- a test that unconditionally raises on a parameter-encoding bug before ever reaching its real assertion (case 3) is not a runnable test of what it claims to test, and a test whose own claimed 'genuine, reliable' induction technique fails 3/3 real attempts (case 1) has not been shown to genuinely exercise the :pending_detach branch at all in this state. Case 2 additionally surfaces that the underlying implementation does not yet satisfy AC3/EO-002 for the exact fixture shape (a keep_forever row inside the retiring month) the design's own EO-002 test shape calls for -- this is Unblock-Everything territory (a defect discovered while validating, not this gate's to silently pass over), but it is not resolved by reworking TEST-DESIGNER's test code alone; ELIXIR-DEV/CODE-DESIGNER need to resolve the 4.4a/4.4b-vs-step-4 ordering contradiction in lib/letflow/event_store/partition_maintenance.ex and/or the design doc.
result.next_action: Rework TEST-DESIGNER (Step 3): (a) fix the correction-(a) test's raw-SQL UUID parameter (bind Ecto.UUID.dump!(event.event_id) or query via the Event schema/Ecto.Query instead of Repo.query!/3's untyped raw SQL) -- deterministic bug, must be fixed regardless of anything else; (b) either add real synchronization to the :pending_detach induction (e.g. have the holder Task explicitly signal -- send a message, or use a Task.await on an intermediate ack -- once its Repo.transaction/1 has actually issued its SELECT and is holding its snapshot, before the detacher Task is started) so the test reliably reaches the interrupted state, or fall back to the design doc's own named alternative ('directly assert against pg_inherits.inhdetachpending if the test harness can't reliably induce the interrupted state', design doc §4.3.3 sub-case 2) and state explicitly in the spec why genuine induction was abandoned; (c) report the EO-002/attach-precondition contradiction (design doc §4.4's 4.4b-then-4.4a ordering vs. §4.3.3 step 4's own ATTACH precondition, for a keep_forever row inside the retiring month) to ORCH as a blocking defect in lib/letflow/event_store/partition_maintenance.ex (and/or the design doc) for ELIXIR-DEV/CODE-DESIGNER rework -- this is not something TEST-DESIGNER's own rework can resolve by rewriting the test, since the test's current failure is correct behavior given the actual (buggy) implementation. Do not mark REQ-376's AC3/EO-002 coverage complete until this is resolved and the EO-002 test passes against a corrected implementation.

issues.description: test/letflow/event_store/partition_maintenance_test.exs's 'correction (a)' test (line ~772) fails deterministically (3/3 runs, all seeds) with DBConnection.EncodeError on its own raw-SQL tableoid lookup at line 794 -- event.event_id (a UUID string) is passed as a bind parameter to Repo.query!/3's raw SQL without dumping it to its 16-byte binary form first, which Ecto.Query's schema casting would normally do automatically but Repo.query!/3 does not. The test can never pass as written, regardless of implementation correctness.

test/letflow/event_store/partition_maintenance_test.exs's ':pending_detach' crash-recovery induction (line ~581) is not reliable -- failed 3/3 independent runs (seeds 0, 1, 42) against real Postgres 16, with two different failure modes, because the holder Task and detacher Task have no synchronization guaranteeing the holder's transaction/snapshot is actually open before the detach begins. The handoff's own claim that this 'actually produces pg_inherits.inhdetachpending = true reliably' is not supported by re-running it.

test/letflow/event_store/partition_maintenance_test.exs's EO-002 test (line ~647) fails deterministically (3/3 runs) with a real Postgres check_violation from lib/letflow/event_store/partition_maintenance.ex's attach_partition!/4 -- a genuine implementation/design defect (§4.4's 4.4b-then-4.4a step-1 ordering leaves a keep_forever row's 4.4a relocation sitting in events_archive_default, in-range, at the moment step 4's ATTACH runs, directly contradicting step 4's own stated precondition that events_archive_default hold no in-range row at ATTACH time) rather than a test-design flaw -- the test is correctly written and correctly catches this. Needs ELIXIR-DEV/CODE-DESIGNER rework of lib/letflow/event_store/partition_maintenance.ex (and/or the design doc's §4.4 ordering), not a TEST-DESIGNER-side fix. Should be reported to ORCH as its own blocking finding per ISSUE_QUEUE.md if not resolved directly in this run's rework loop.
